description: Refers successful loading zone pilot update to Accessibility Advisory Committee.
New policy establishes process for accessible loading zones.
Eligible locations include schools, health facilities, community services.
Residential locations are excluded; zones are 6-10 meters long.
Signage restricts use to vehicles with accessible placards.

chips.text: Received as information
Cost of accessibility ramp is up to the applicant to cover.
Pilot project participants expressed high satisfaction with new accessible loading zones.
Improved access for people using mobility devices to buildings.

description: City reviews 2% target for accessible loading zones.
May add more accessible spots if current provision is insufficient.

chips.text: Councillor questions 2% accessible parking target, suggests 4-5% needed.
Public speaker supports loading zones, notes frustration with misuse.
Dedicated loading zones improve accessibility for people with disabilities.
Staff promises to revisit 2% accessible parking target if insufficient.

description: Increases on-street accessible parking in pay zones.
Sets design standards and location criteria for new spaces.
Prioritizes snow removal for accessible parking and ramps.
Committee seeks more feedback for a March review.

chips.text: Approved
Committee found the proposed 2% cap on Broadway insufficient.
Out-of-town visitors and regional users of city services.
Data on local accessible parking placard usage is not yet available.
Public speaker expressed strong support for accessible loading zones.
Accessible parking demand may be higher than the 2% proposed cap.
Staff committed to revisiting the 2% accessible parking cap.

description: Set 2026 Work Plan categories for transit, accessibility, safety, education.
